sanjay: Heads-up: ECC correctable spike on eu-west gpu-pool-12. 15m error rate ~18/hr per affected card, baseline ~0.5/hr. Grafana: https://grafana.internal/r/abc123 :eyes:
oncall-bot: Alert INC-5422 created for gpu-pool-12 (severity: warning)
alex: Which nodes are noisy? any XIDs/OOMs or PCIe resets?
sanjay: Nodes: gpu-node-eu-123, gpu-node-eu-127, gpu-node-eu-129, gpu-node-eu-131, gpu-node-eu-134, gpu-node-eu-138. No driver OOMs yet; seeing repeated correctable ECC bursts and a few pcie reset hints. sample dmesg snippet:
```
[  512.345678] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: Correctable ECC error detected
[  512.345679] NVRM: Xid (0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
[  512.345680] pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: AER: Corrected error received: id 00e0
```
kevin: Running gpunodectl health --nodes gpu-node-eu-12[3,7,9,11,14,18] now. If counts keep trending up I'll initiate soft-drain on top 3.
kevin: (output) gpu-node-eu-123: 42 correctables/15m, gpu-node-eu-127: 37, gpu-node-eu-129: 5, others 10-20.
maria: Our current auto-drain soft threshold is 100 correctables/hr per card (global). For eu-west we should be more conservative while we investigate. Propose: soft_threshold=40/hr, hard_threshold=120/hr, window=10m, require sustained for 2 windows before action. This reduces blast while catching real regressions. :thinking_face:
alex: Lowering threshold will increase churn and replacement ops. Can we do tiered actions instead? e.g. soft-drain at 40/hr -> route new pods off node but keep existing pinned, escalate to hard-drain+replacement at 120/hr or if soft-drain happens 3 times in 24h. That limits spurious evictions.
kevin: Agree. Also suggest marking dedicated/reserved pools as exempt from auto-eviction (customers with pinned workloads). Add a quota for daily evictions per-region to cap cost.
sanjay: I ran a quick sim: rwdctl simulate-decision --pool gpu-pool-12 --window 10m --soft 40 --hard 120 -> predicted evictions: 5 nodes over 6h under current spike profile. CPU/throughput impact ~2% after routing to spare-capacity pool. Output:
```
SIM: events=6 nodes_flagged=5 predicted_evictions=5 spare_pool_headroom=8%
```
maria: Short-term mitigation idea: temporarily enable kernel ECC suppressions/threshold scaling in driver? meh, risky. Better: roll driver to known-good (e.g., nv-driver 525.105) on a small canary set and see if correctables drop.
kevin: I'll push a canary monitor config change to the controller: soft_threshold=40, hard_threshold=120, window=10m, sustained=2. Also enable routing-rule to shift batch workloads to dedicated-spare-eu for 30m. Deploying canary to 2 nodes now. :hammer:
infra-alert-bot: CR-7893 created: "eu-west gpu auto-drain tuning + canary driver rollback plan". Links: https://infra.internal/cr/7893
sanjay: If hard drains start we escalate to HW replacement and SRE oncall. Also open HWR ticket with vendors for impacted serials. For now watch delta in PCIe resets; set escalation at 70% of hard_threshold (i.e., 84/hr) to get eyes sooner. I'll stay on watch for the next 2h. :white_check_mark:
